plan.title: Time-course DESeq2 LRT: treatment-specific trajectory genes
plan.analytical_narrative: The design is 2 conditions x 4 time points (t0-t3), n=3 per cell, raw salmon gene counts (12000 genes x 25 samples; metadata has condition, time, time_hours). The question — which genes change over time in a treatment-specific way, beyond the shared time trend — is exactly the DESeq2 time-course likelihood-ratio-test scenario: fit the full model ~condition + time + condition:time against the reduced model ~condition + time. A gene significant under this LRT has a time trajectory that differs between conditions, independent of any time effect shared by both. Track T1 runs sample-structure QC, minimal count filtering, the LRT itself, apeglm/ashr-based shrinkage of the per-timepoint interaction coefficients, BH-adjusted results, and trajectory clustering of the hits. Track T2 takes the LRT statistic ranking into fgsea preranked enrichment against MSigDB Hallmark (staged locally) with Reactome as a confirmatory second pass. A final report step assembles diagnostics, the interaction/simple-effect tables, the trajectory clusters, and the enrichment results with the mandatory power caveat: n=3/cell gives an interaction test with low power, so absence from the hit list is not evidence of no treatment-specific effect.

steps.method: DESeq2 vst(blind) PCA, sample distance heatmap, library size QC
Minimal pre-filter: keep genes with >=10 counts in >= smallest group size (n=3)
DESeq2 design ~condition + time + condition:time, explicit reference levels, LRT full vs reduced (~condition+time)
DESeq2 likelihood ratio test (interaction, time course >=3 timepoints)
apeglm shrinkage of per-timepoint interaction/simple-effect coefficients
Benjamini-Hochberg FDR with independent filtering, alpha=0.05
fgsea preranked GSEA on Wald/LRT stat, MSigDB Hallmark then Reactome
Trajectory clustering of significant genes, simple effects + interaction contrast tables, power caveat, diagnostics
